result: In transgenic and knockout mice, WASF3 disrupted complex IV, localized to mitochondria-associated membranes, shifted hippocampal metabolism toward glycolysis, lowered ATPIF1 and impaired learning, while WASF3 deficiency enhanced oxidative metabolism and preserved cognition under stress.
reason: Same WASF3 complex-IV mechanism in mice, extended from muscle/exercise to brain metabolism and cognition; not the cited Wang 2023 paper; animal-only.

result: In 34 PCC-with-fatigue vs 37 recovered controls, neurocognitive and immune markers were within normal ranges, with only modest white-matter, myelin-related and global brain differences and altered connectivity-performance associations.
reason: Reports white-matter/myelin and network connectivity, not thalamus, basal ganglia or choroid plexus structure; long COVID version of white-matter finding; abstract gives no effect sizes.

result: In 206 SARS-CoV-2-infected participants, concentrations of autoantibodies against 13 neurotransmitter-related receptors did not differ between new-onset post-COVID fatigue, pre-existing fatigue and non-fatigued controls, and did not track fatigue severity or reference-value positivity.
reason: Null result agrees with the finding as phrased (elevation not reproduced), so it replicates rather than contradicts; post-COVID fatigue population, commercial binding assays.

result: In 442 COVID-19 patients (184 followed at ~3.2 months), plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected in 67.4% at baseline and 53.6% at follow-up, was associated with critical acute illness, but neither baseline nor follow-up RNAemia nor its trajectory was associated with PCC.
reason: Circulating viral RNA rather than antigen, but same mechanism of blood viral persistence; supports the severity link and adds a null for PCC association; mostly hospitalised cohort, no pre-pandemic controls.

result: In 82 of 102 PCS patients followed for 6 months, CRAE rose from 178.2 to 184.1 um and AVR from 0.83 to 0.86 toward recovered-control values, while venular dysfunction persisted.
reason: Same retinal vessel analysis measures in the same cohort as Wallraven 2026, adding a time course (arteriolar convergence, persistent venular deficit); not independent, abstract truncated.

result: iPSC-derived myotubes from 6 ME/CFS patients vs 7 controls showed 3 differentially expressed genes (ERVH48-1, CDX4, SLC2A14), 16 isoform-switching genes and pathway changes in proteostasis and mitochondrial quality control.
reason: Transcriptomics of iPSC myotubes, not AMPK activation or glucose uptake after EPS; no atlas finding covers myotube transcriptomes; very small sample (possible new muscle item).

result: In 9 immunodeficient long-COVID ME/CFS patients with circulating spike, median spike fell from 63 to 26 pg/ml after tixagevimab/cilgavimab but not significantly (p=0.63), with no significant clinical change at 30 days.
reason: Measures plasma spike and adds a treatment-response observation like the nirmatrelvir note in the detail; tiny, uncontrolled, does not test prevalence vs controls.

result: After tixagevimab/cilgavimab in 9 patients, beta1-adrenergic autoantibodies fell from 26.8 to 21.2 U/ml (unadjusted p=0.003) while beta2 and M3/M4 antibodies did not change.
reason: Does not compare antibody levels with controls, so does not test the elevation claim; the only change is in beta1, outside the claim; n=9, uncontrolled, unadjusted p.

result: In an adaptive placebo-controlled RCT of 399 long-COVID adults with fatigue in Brazil, fluvoxamine 100 mg BID lowered FSS vs placebo by 0.43 at day 60 and 0.58 at day 90 (posterior probability of superiority 99%) and improved quality of life; metformin was inconclusive and stopped for futility.
reason: Trials domain: a large RCT of fluvoxamine and metformin in long COVID that the atlas does not cover; related to but distinct from trials-ssri (fluoxetine in CFS, null).

result: In 44 long COVID vs 44 controls, somatosensory processing did not differ (multivariate P=0.172) or change after cognitive or physical exertion, performance fatigability did not differ (P=0.199-0.441), and resting HRV was lower in long COVID but not associated with fatigue.
reason: Somatosensory attenuation is not the light/sound sensitivity or ERP measure in neuro-sensory; lower resting HRV is a long COVID version of neuro-hrv, and the fatigability null bears on motor fatigability.
